note.explanation: Physics provides scientific principles used in technology and engineering. Technology uses scientific knowledge to develop methods and techniques. Engineering applies scientific principles and technologies to design and build things for specific needs, while also considering cost and safety.
examples: Automobile technology is based on the principles of thermodynamics.
A civil engineer designs bridges to withstand strong winds, earthquakes, intense weather conditions and heavy traffic.
note.checkAnswer: Automobile technology is based on thermodynamics.
note.simple: Science helps us understand how things work. Technology uses that knowledge to make methods, machines or programmes. Engineering uses scientific knowledge and technology to design useful things.

written.text: Differentiate the terms, science, technology and engineering with examples.
written.finalAnswer: Science is a collective knowledge about natural phenomena and events. Technology refers to methods and techniques developed by using scientific knowledge; for example, automobile technology is based on thermodynamics. Engineering is the process of applying technologies and scientific principles to design instruments, tools and other things for specific needs; for example, a civil engineer designs a bridge to withstand heavy traffic and severe weather.

modelAnswer: Science is a collective knowledge about the natural phenomena and events.
Technology refers to the methods and techniques developed by using scientific knowledge; for example, automobile technology is based on the principles of thermodynamics.
Engineering is the process of applying various technologies and scientific principles to design various instruments, tools and build things that help to meet specific needs.
For example, a civil engineer designs a bridge that can withstand strong winds, earthquakes, intense weather conditions and heavy traffic.

examTips: Expect short questions that ask you to state the scientific basis of a technology, such as laser, radar or automobile technology.
A question comparing science, technology and engineering needs a clear definition of each term and a relevant example.
For questions about engineers' jobs, name the job and describe what is designed and the need or condition it addresses.
Use the exact links given in your textbook: automobile technology—thermodynamics; radar—electromagnetic waves; laser—atomic physics.
When describing engineering, include that engineers consider cost effectiveness and safety measures.

explain.title: Physics supports technology
explain.body: Science or to be more specific, Physics plays a vital role being the core of each invention based on physical laws and principles. Technology refers to the methods and techniques developed by using scientific knowledge.

explain.title: Technologies use different principles
explain.body: Automobile technology is based on the principles of the thermodynamics. Radar technology is based on the detection and reflection principles of electromagnetic waves. Laser technology is based on the principles of atomic physics.

explain.title: Engineering designs for needs
explain.body: Engineering is the process of applying various technologies and scientific principles to design various instruments, tools and build things that help to meet specific needs in every walk of life. Engineers also consider factors like cost effectiveness and safety measures when designing various products.

explain.title: The fields work together
explain.body: Scientific discoveries lead to new technologies and engineers rely on scientific knowledge for our benefits and comforts. These fields work together to help change how people live.

mistakes: Mixing up the scientific bases: automobile technology is linked with thermodynamics, radar with electromagnetic waves and laser with atomic physics.
Defining technology only as a machine; your textbook also says technology may be a software programme of information technology.
Describing engineering as just building things, without mentioning the application of technologies and scientific principles to meet specific needs.
Forgetting that engineers consider cost effectiveness and safety measures.
Giving an engineer's job title without explaining what the engineer designs or what conditions the design must handle.
